body:
Found while triaging the CultureMech unresolved residual. Evidence table:
`reports/culturemech_ambiguous_identifiers.tsv` (written by
`scripts/triage_culturemech_residual.py`).

55 CultureMech surface forms (383 recipe mentions) fold onto a MIM label that **two or
more records publish**. CultureMech fails closed on an ambiguous `label_index` row, so
each of these is an unresolvable ingredient — and unlike a plain miss, it cannot be fixed
by adding a spelling, because the question "which record owns this name?" has no answer
yet.

Ranked by affected mentions:

| mentions | identifier set |
|---:|---|
| 141 | `MICRO:0001647` / `NCIT:C75874` (Sea Salt) |
| 95 | `FOODON:03315719` / `mesh:C017721` (Casamino acids) |
| 34 | `MICRO:0000460` + 5 `kgmicrobe.ingredient:*` vitamin solutions |
| 28 | `FOODON:03315719` / `MICRO:0000182` (Pancreatic digest of casein) |
| 19 | `CHEBI:17439` / `CHEBI:176843` (Vitamin B12) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:3312` / `CHEBI:86158` (CaCl2 2H2O) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:91247` / `kgmicrobe.ingredient:l-cysteine_x_hcl_x_h2o_solution` |
| 10 | `CHEBI:31795` / `CHEBI:32599` (MgSO4 7H2O) |
| 5 | `CHEBI:35696` / `kgmicrobe.compound:cocl2_x_2_h2o` / `cocl2_x_4_h2o` |
| 3 | `CHEBI:17909` / `CHEBI:26833` (sulfur) |

These are not all one defect. At least three kinds are mixed here, and they want different
answers:

1. **Duplicate records on one substance** — `Sea Salt`, `Casamino acids`. A merge under the
   `merge-ingredients` skill.
2. **Granularity disagreement** — `CHEBI:17909` (sulfur atom) vs `CHEBI:26833` (elemental
   sulfur); `CHEBI:17439` (cyanocobalamin) vs `CHEBI:176843` (cobalamin). A decision under
   MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3, not a merge.
3. **A wrong synonym on a hydrate sibling, which is an identity error rather than an
   ambiguity.** `CoCl2 6H2O` matches records for the **di**- and **tetra**-hydrate, so
   those records carry a hexahydrate spelling they do not denote. Same shape for
   `CaCl2 2H2O` against `CHEBI:3312`, which is anhydrous calcium chloride. Hydration state
   is identity (MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3): these synonyms should be removed regardless
   of how the ambiguity is resolved.

Kind 3 is the one worth doing first -- it is a wrong claim now being published, whereas
kinds 1 and 2 are unresolved questions.

Not addressed in the grounding PR that found this: resolving these needs per-family
judgement, and the PR deliberately skips every shared identifier rather than picking an
owner arbitrarily.
title: 25 identifier sets publish the same ingredient label under two or more records

body:
Surfaced by #167, which made the collection headers honest: `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml` now reports **1877 MAPPED + 2 non-MAPPED** against `total_count: 1879`. Previously the header claimed `mapped_count: 1877 / unmapped_count: 0` against 1879 records — self-inconsistent, so the 2 were invisible.

The 2 are `data/ingredients/mapped/Bacto_Soytone.yaml` and `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_L-lactate.yaml`. Both have **two** problems.

## 1. `mapping_status: REJECTED` but filed under `mapped/`

Both carry `mapping_status: REJECTED` while living in `data/ingredients/mapped/` and appearing in `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml`. Either the rejection should move them to `unmapped/`, or the status is wrong.

## 2. The record `identifier` contradicts its own `ontology_mapping`

Per `docs/CURIE_STANDARD.md`, in MIM the record `identifier` **is** the ontology mapping CURIE for a mapped record. Neither of these satisfies that:

| file | `identifier` | `ontology_mapping.ontology_id` | problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sodium_L-lactate.yaml` | `CHEBI:867561` | `CHEBI:232798` (sodium L-lactate) | identifier ≠ mapping; **and `867561` exceeds the `CHEBI: 300000` plausibility ceiling** in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, the signature of a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix |
| `Bacto_Soytone.yaml` | `CHEBI:8150` | `FOODON:03315720` ("vegetable protein, hydrolyzed") | identifier ≠ mapping, and the **prefixes disagree** — identifier says CHEBI, mapping says FOODON |

The `CHEBI:232798` and `FOODON:03315720` mappings both look correct; it is the `identifier` that is stale or wrong in each case.

## Why the plausibility gate did not catch `CHEBI:867561`

The id↔label gate validates `(ontology_id, ontology_label)` pairs. The bogus value is in the `identifier` field, which is not part of a validated pair — so an out-of-ceiling CHEBI can sit in the primary key indefinitely. Worth considering whether `identifier` should be range-checked too, given that in MIM it is by definition an ontology CURIE.

## Related

`Bacto_Soytone`'s mapping target `FOODON:03315720` is the same term already carried by `Phytone` and `Soya_Pepton` (see the duplicate-primary-key item in `NEXT_TASKS.md`), so resolving this should be coordinated with that dedup.
title: REJECTED and PENDING_REVIEW records sit in data/ingredients/mapped/ — 29 of them now

body:
Surfaced while curating PR #145. Not caused by that work; filing so it is not lost.

## What
The curated collections (`data/curated/{mapped,unmapped}_ingredients.yaml`) and the per-record corpus (`data/ingredients/{mapped,unmapped}/*.yaml`) have drifted apart on `main` in several ways:

1. **Stale per-record files never re-exported.** Running `just export-individual` regenerates ~59 per-record files with content the collection already had (corrected mappings, curation notes) that the committed per-record files lack. The per-record files lag the collection.

2. **Duplicate-state records.** At least 3 records — `Phytone` (UNMAPPED_0488), `Soya_Pepton` (UNMAPPED_0531), `Tryptone_Peptone` (UNMAPPED_0558) — are listed as **UNMAPPED** in the collection but have a **mapped/** per-record file on disk. Re-exporting creates an `unmapped/` file for each while the stale `mapped/` file persists → the same identifier exists in two states/dirs.

## Why it matters
`aggregate-collections` (per-record -> collection) and `export-individual` (collection -> per-record) are supposed to be inverses, but the corpus and collection disagree, so a round-trip is not idempotent. The duplicate-state records are the worst case — a consumer reading the per-record tree sees a different mapping_status than one reading the collection.

## Suggested fix
A dedicated resync pass: pick the collection as canonical, run `export-individual`, delete orphaned stale per-record files, verify with `reconcile_sssom` + `validate-strict`, commit as its own reviewable PR. Do this **after** the filename-casing footgun #147 is fixed, since `export-individual` is the tool involved and would otherwise bake in the casing drift.
title: Pre-existing collection<->per-record drift (stale mapped/ files, duplicate-state records)
